newsitem.title: USA: New catastrophe loss index created by Calif. firm.
newsitem.headline: New catastrophe loss index created by Calif. firm.

text.p: Risk Management Solutions said it has created a new financial index for use by issuers and investors involved in securities trading based on insured catastrophe risk.
The index, called the RMS CAT Index, will be published and widely available before the start of the U.S. hurricane season in June, the Menlo Park, Calif-based company said.
Risk Management said it expects the index to be used as the basis for structuring, pricing and trading both securities and certain traditional reinsurance contracts.
Risk Management said its index offers several advantages over existing indexes, including timeliness of reporting and objectivity of approach.

"Investors have expressed a lack of comfort with potential conflict of interest issues and with the time delays that are inherent in existing indexes based on reported losses," said Rob McCormack, director of the capital markets group at Risk Management.

Risk Management said its index will overcome these issues by relying on objective loss modeling and predefined industry exposure data by ZIP Code to deliver estimates of the losses from earthquakes and hurricanes seven days following each event.
"We have been keenly involved with the securitization movement from the start," Risk Management president Tom Hutton said.
"Our intent is to provide a facilitating mechanism that benefits the whole market, both here in the U.S. and internationally."

Risk Management said it will hold informational seminars on the index beginning in late April and is actively seeking appropriate channels for publication of the index, including its own Internet site.
